decision_lens: Prioritize whether 4 teammates produce genuinely independent 'sights' on the spec corpus or co-vary because of shared training/prompting. Critique anchoring-bias claims by asking whether the proposed mesh actually breaks the bias or just hides it across more agents.
distance_rationale: A maritime practical-mathematics tradition predating electronic computation, focused on independent-sight triangulation under irreducible measurement uncertainty, with no surface overlap to LLM agents.
expected_isomorphisms: The three-bearing fix transfers as a cross-cluster-independence requirement that clustering must satisfy, not just within-cluster coherence. The cocked-hat-rejection transfers as a divergence-threshold escape rule for the synthesis lead.
focus: Three-body fix from independent sights to escape a single-bearing anchor — establishing a position by intersecting cross-bearings under uncertainty and a cost-bounded sight budget
name: fd-celestial-navigation-fix
persona: Apply the perspective of a celestial navigator working a sextant and chronometer who needs to fix a ship's position from three star sights — knowing that one sight gives a line of position but not a fix, two sights give a fix that may be biased by unknown current, and three or four well-distributed sights let the navigator detect inconsistency and refuse a bad fix rather than commit to a wrong heading.
review_areas: Whether the 3 domain debaters are clustered to maximise independence (distant source_domains across debaters) or could end up holding correlated clusters that all triangulate to the same wrong answer
Whether the lead's synthesis acts like a navigator plotting intersecting LOPs and rejecting a fix when the cocked-hat is too large, or just averages the loudest debaters
Whether there is a 'cocked hat' equivalent — a divergence threshold above which the lead refuses to write a synthesis and reports inconsistency instead of forcing closure
Whether the anchoring-bias argument actually addresses correlated-error-across-sights (all four agents trained on overlapping data) rather than just sequential-context bias

Whether the plan-time A/B comparison treats the subagent path as a single-LOP baseline and the teams path as a true triangulation, or whether the comparison is symmetric and misses the structural claim
Whether the cluster-by-source_domain-similarity assignment risks the opposite of independence (a cluster of similar agents collapses to one effective sight)

severity_examples.condition: The clustering rule prioritizes within-cluster coherence without enforcing across-cluster distance
severity_examples.scenario: Cluster-by-similarity in §3 produces three debaters whose source_domains are tightly correlated, so triangulation is illusory and anchoring bias re-enters through cluster choice

severity_examples.condition: The 2-round TaskCompleted enforcement does not distinguish 'time up, converged' from 'time up, divergent'
severity_examples.scenario: The lead has no escape hatch when debaters disagree irreconcilably and is forced to write synthesis from divergent material

severity_examples.condition: Open Question 1's reviewer agent scores synthesis quality on surface features rather than on isomorphism-not-found-by-subagent
severity_examples.scenario: A/B benchmark treats teams-vs-subagent symmetrically rather than as fix-vs-single-bearing, missing the test that matters: does teams catch errors subagent commits to?

success_hints: Enforce across-cluster distance, not within-cluster coherence
Audit cluster correlation at plan time
task_context: Reviewing a brainstorm whose central claim is that 4-teammate debate breaks the anchoring bias of single-Sonnet synthesis. Looking for whether the proposed clustering and synthesis rules actually achieve independent triangulation.
